title: Milieuschutz in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has 82 social preservation areas covering 5,318 hectares.** Mitte and Pankow hold 14 each, Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg 11, Tempelhof-Schöneberg and Neukölln 10 each. Marzahn-Hellersdorf has none. **68 per cent of Berlin's housing stock sits outside them.**

**Inside an area, demolition, structural change and change of use all need a borough permit,** under section 172 of the Baugesetzbuch. The permit is separate from any building-code approval and it covers empty flats and owner-occupied ones too.

**One city-wide rulebook now decides what gets refused.** The VV Genehmigungskriterien came into force on **18 April 2026**. Refused outright: demolition, merging or splitting flats, changing a home to another use, and high-value fittings such as underfloor heating, a fireplace, high-grade parquet or floor-to-ceiling windows.

**A first bathroom and a first small balcony have to be approved.** A second bathroom, a second WC or a second balcony does not, unless the flat has at least five habitable rooms. In a building of four floors or fewer, a new lift is not approvable at all.

**Converting rentals to condominiums needs permission across all of Berlin** for any building with more than five flats, from **1 January 2026 to 31 December 2030**. Completed conversions fell from **28,783 flats in 2021 to 1,552 in 2024**.

**After a conversion and sale, a buyer cannot claim own-use for ten years.** Berlin's Kündigungsschutzklausel-Verordnung took over on **1 October 2023** and applies city-wide, not only inside the 82 areas.

**Furnished fixed-term letting inside the areas now needs a permit.** Furnished short-term listings went from **13 per cent of Berlin ads in 2012 to 48 per cent in 2025**, median asking rent **€14.37 to €24.12 per square metre**. The Verwaltungsgericht Berlin backed the rule on **10 September 2026**.
